items.subject: eng

skill.en: Responding to a 'Would you mind…?' request
skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอที่ใช้ Would you mind…?

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Would you mind if I opened the window? It's really stuffy in here.
B: ______ Go ahead.

explanation.en: "Would you mind…?" asks whether you object, so "Not at all" (= I don't mind) agrees, which fits "Go ahead". "Yes, I would" refuses; "Never mind" dismisses a problem; "No, thanks" declines an offer.
explanation.th: Would you mind…? ถามว่าเรารังเกียจหรือไม่ การตอบ Not at all แปลว่า ไม่รังเกียจเลย จึงเข้ากับ Go ahead ส่วน Yes, I would เป็นการปฏิเสธ Never mind ใช้บอกว่าไม่เป็นไร และ No, thanks ใช้ปฏิเสธข้อเสนอ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอโทษ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I'm so sorry I'm late. The bus broke down on the expressway.
B: ______ We haven't started the meeting yet.

explanation.en: "Don't worry about it" accepts an apology. "You're welcome" and "It's my pleasure" answer thanks, not an apology; "Same to you" returns a wish.
explanation.th: Don't worry about it ใช้ตอบรับคำขอโทษ ส่วน You're welcome และ It's my pleasure ใช้ตอบคำขอบคุณ และ Same to you ใช้อวยพรกลับ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Giving advice with 'If I were you'
skill.th: การให้คำแนะนำด้วย If I were you

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I can't decide whether to join the robotics club or the debate team.
B: ______ You love building things, and you always say debating makes you nervous.
choices: Why don't you choose debate, then?
I'd rather you didn't join anything.
Either way, it's none of my business.
If I were you, I'd go for robotics.

explanation.en: B's reasons (loves building things, debating makes A nervous) support robotics, so "If I were you, I'd go for robotics" fits. Suggesting debate contradicts the reasons; the other two do not give the advice A asked for.
explanation.th: เหตุผลที่ B ให้ (ชอบประดิษฐ์ และกลัวการโต้วาที) สนับสนุนชมรมหุ่นยนต์ จึงตอบ If I were you, I'd go for robotics การแนะนำให้เลือก debate ขัดกับเหตุผล ส่วนอีกสองตัวเลือกไม่ได้ให้คำแนะนำ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การบอกผลว่าสิ่งใดเป็นอย่างไร

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: How did your presentation go this morning?
B: ______ I forgot half of what I wanted to say.
A: Oh no. I'm sure it wasn't as bad as you think.
choices: I'm going to present it soon.
Not very well, to be honest.

explanation.en: B forgot half the speech and A comforts B, so B must say it went badly: "Not very well, to be honest". "It went like a dream" means it went perfectly; the future forms ignore that the presentation is already over.
explanation.th: B ลืมสิ่งที่จะพูดไปครึ่งหนึ่ง และ A ปลอบใจ จึงต้องตอบว่าไม่ค่อยดี Not very well, to be honest ส่วน It went like a dream แปลว่าราบรื่นมาก และรูปอนาคตไม่เข้ากับเหตุการณ์ที่ผ่านไปแล้ว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเข้าใจสำนวนในบริบท

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Did you finish the science project on time?
B: Only just. We handed it in five minutes before the deadline.
A: Wow, ______
choices: that was a piece of cake!
you must have got cold feet!

explanation.en: "Cutting it fine" means leaving almost no spare time, exactly what five minutes before the deadline shows. "A piece of cake" means very easy, "get cold feet" means become too nervous to do something, and "on cloud nine" means extremely happy.
explanation.th: cutting it fine แปลว่าเฉียดฉิวแทบไม่เหลือเวลา ตรงกับการส่งงานก่อนหมดเวลา 5 นาที ส่วน a piece of cake แปลว่าง่ายมาก get cold feet แปลว่าเกิดกลัวจนไม่กล้าทำ และ on cloud nine แปลว่ามีความสุขมาก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I think the school should ban phones completely during lessons.
B: ______ Some teachers use phones for quizzes and research, so a total ban might do more harm than good.
choices: I couldn't agree with you more.
I see your point, but I'm not entirely convinced.
That's exactly what I was going to say.

explanation.en: B goes on to argue against a total ban, so B must disagree politely: "I see your point, but I'm not entirely convinced". The other three all express strong agreement, which contradicts what B says next.
explanation.th: ประโยคต่อมาของ B แย้งการห้ามใช้โทรศัพท์ทั้งหมด จึงต้องเป็นการไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ I see your point, but I'm not entirely convinced อีกสามตัวเลือกล้วนแสดงการเห็นด้วยอย่างยิ่ง จึงขัดกับสิ่งที่ B พูดต่อ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Phrasal verbs: fill in a form
skill.th: กริยาวลี fill in

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Please ______ the form and hand it to the officer at the counter."

explanation.en: We "fill in" (or fill out) a form, meaning write the required information. "Fill up" is for containers or petrol tanks; "fill on" does not exist; "fill with" needs a material (fill a box with books).
explanation.th: กรอกแบบฟอร์มใช้ fill in (หรือ fill out) ส่วน fill up ใช้กับการเติมให้เต็ม เช่น ถังน้ำมัน fill on ไม่มีใช้ และ fill with ต้องตามด้วยสิ่งที่ใส่

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วม strong demand

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Thailand's durian exports rose sharply last year because of strong ______ from China."

explanation.en: "Strong demand" is the fixed business collocation for how much buyers want a product. "Request" and "requirement" are not used for market buying, and "desire" is personal, not commercial.
explanation.th: strong demand เป็นคำปรากฏร่วมทางเศรษฐกิจ หมายถึงความต้องการซื้อสูง ส่วน request, requirement ไม่ใช้กับความต้องการของตลาด และ desire เป็นความปรารถนาส่วนตัว

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Word formation: noun from a verb
skill.th: การสร้างคำนามจากกริยา

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The volunteers showed great ______ when they kept working through the heavy rain."

explanation.en: After the adjective "great" and the verb "showed" we need a noun: "determination". "Determine" is a verb and "determined"/"determining" are adjective or participle forms.
explanation.th: หลัง showed great ต้องใช้คำนาม คือ determination (ความมุ่งมั่น) ส่วน determine เป็นกริยา determined และ determining เป็นคุณศัพท์หรือ participle

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำที่มีความหมายใกล้เคียงตามบริบท

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to "reluctant".
"The new manager was reluctant to change the timetable so close to the exams."

explanation.en: "Reluctant" means not wanting to do something, so "unwilling" is the synonym. "Eager" is the opposite; "careless" and "proud" describe other qualities.
explanation.th: reluctant แปลว่าไม่เต็มใจ ตรงกับ unwilling ส่วน eager มีความหมายตรงข้าม (กระตือรือร้น) และ careless, proud มีความหมายอื่น

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลี call off

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The concert had to be ______ because the singer had lost her voice."

explanation.en: "Call off" means cancel, which is what happens when the singer cannot sing. "Call on" means visit or ask someone to speak, "put up" means build or give someone a place to stay, and "take off" means remove or leave the ground.
explanation.th: call off แปลว่ายกเลิก ตรงกับสถานการณ์ที่นักร้องเสียงหาย ส่วน call on แปลว่าแวะเยี่ยมหรือเรียกให้พูด put up แปลว่าสร้างหรือให้ที่พัก และ take off แปลว่าถอดหรือขึ้นบิน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วมกับ attention

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Although the documentary was very long, it never failed to ______ my attention."

explanation.en: Something interesting "holds your attention" (keeps you interested). We "pay attention" ourselves, but a film cannot pay my attention; "spend" and "make" do not collocate with attention.
explanation.th: สิ่งที่น่าสนใจจะ hold your attention คือดึงความสนใจไว้ได้ เราเป็นผู้ pay attention เอง แต่สารคดีไม่สามารถ pay my attention ได้ ส่วน spend และ make ไม่ใช้กับ attention

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเดาความหมายจากคำบ่งชี้ที่ขัดแย้งกัน

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the meaning closest to "frugal" in the sentence.
"Unlike her brother, who is quite frugal, Nida spends money freely on clothes and gadgets."

explanation.en: "Unlike" sets up a contrast with someone who spends money freely, so "frugal" must mean careful with money. "Generous" points the wrong way, and laziness or honesty has nothing to do with spending.
explanation.th: Unlike แสดงความขัดแย้งกับคนที่ใช้เงินฟุ่มเฟือย ดังนั้น frugal ต้องแปลว่าประหยัด ใช้เงินอย่างระมัดระวัง ส่วน generous (ใจกว้าง) มีทิศทางตรงข้าม และความขี้เกียจหรือความซื่อสัตย์ไม่เกี่ยวกับการใช้เงิน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสร้างคำด้วยอุปสรรคปฏิเสธ

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Many people think the plan is ______ because it would cost far more than the city can afford."

explanation.en: The negative form of "realistic" is "unrealistic". "Ir-" is used before r (irregular, irresponsible) but not with realistic; "dis-" and "non-" do not combine with this word.
explanation.th: คำปฏิเสธของ realistic คือ unrealistic ส่วน ir- ใช้กับบางคำที่ขึ้นต้นด้วย r เช่น irregular แต่ไม่ใช้กับ realistic และ dis-, non- ไม่ใช้กับคำนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: สำนวนตายตัว cast doubt on

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The scientist's findings ______ doubt on a theory that had been accepted for decades."

explanation.en: The fixed expression is "cast doubt on something" (make people less sure it is true). "Give", "make" and "bring" are not used with doubt in this way.
explanation.th: สำนวนตายตัวคือ cast doubt on something แปลว่าทำให้เกิดความสงสัยในสิ่งนั้น ส่วน gave, made, brought ไม่ใช้กับ doubt ในความหมายนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำที่มักสับสน afford กับ effort

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I'm afraid I can't ______ to buy a new laptop this year; my savings are almost gone."

explanation.en: "Can't afford to buy" means not having enough money, matching "my savings are almost gone". "Effort" is a noun; "spend to buy" and "pay to buy" are not correct patterns.
explanation.th: can't afford to buy แปลว่ามีเงินไม่พอจะซื้อ ตรงกับเงินเก็บใกล้หมด ส่วน effort เป็นคำนาม และ spend to buy, pay to buy ไม่ใช่รูปที่ถูกต้อง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: past perfect กับ by the time

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film ______."

explanation.en: The film started before we arrived, both in the past, so the earlier action takes the past perfect: "had already started". Present perfect and present simple do not fit a past time frame.
explanation.th: หนังเริ่มก่อนที่เราจะมาถึง ซึ่งเป็นอดีตทั้งคู่ เหตุการณ์ที่เกิดก่อนจึงใช้ past perfect คือ had already started ส่วน present perfect และ present simple ไม่เข้ากับกรอบเวลาอดีต

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Present perfect continuous for duration up to now
skill.th: present perfect continuous กับระยะเวลาจนถึงปัจจุบัน

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Sompong is exhausted because he ______ for his exams since six o'clock this morning."

explanation.en: "Since six o'clock" plus a present result (is exhausted) needs the present perfect continuous: "has been revising". Past simple and past perfect cut the link with now; present continuous cannot go with "since".
explanation.th: since six o'clock และผลในปัจจุบัน (is exhausted) ต้องใช้ present perfect continuous คือ has been revising ส่วน past simple และ past perfect ไม่เชื่อมกับปัจจุบัน และ present continuous ใช้กับ since ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result
skill.th: mixed conditional เงื่อนไขอดีต ผลปัจจุบัน

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If I had listened to my coach last season, I ______ in the national team now."

explanation.en: The condition is past (had listened … last season) but the result is present (now), so this is a mixed conditional: "would be". "Would have been" refers to a past result, and "will be"/"had been" break the conditional pattern.
explanation.th: เงื่อนไขอยู่ในอดีต (had listened … last season) แต่ผลอยู่ในปัจจุบัน (now) จึงเป็น mixed conditional ใช้ would be ส่วน would have been ใช้กับผลในอดีต และ will be, had been ผิดรูปประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Wish + past perfect for past regrets
skill.th: wish + past perfect แสดงความเสียดายในอดีต

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I wish I ______ my umbrella at home; now I'm soaking wet."

explanation.en: The regret is about a past action (leaving the umbrella this morning), so wish takes the past perfect: "hadn't left". "Didn't leave" would be for a present wish, and "wouldn't"/"haven't" are not used this way.
explanation.th: เสียดายการกระทำในอดีต (ลืมร่มไว้ที่บ้าน) wish จึงตามด้วย past perfect คือ hadn't left ส่วน didn't leave ใช้กับความปรารถนาในปัจจุบัน และ wouldn't, haven't ไม่ใช้ในโครงสร้างนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: passive กับ modal verb

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"All mobile phones ______ before students enter the examination room."

explanation.en: Phones do not switch themselves off; someone switches them off, so we need modal + be + past participle: "must be switched off". The active forms make the phones the doers.
explanation.th: โทรศัพท์ไม่ได้ปิดตัวเอง แต่ถูกปิด จึงต้องใช้ modal + be + V3 คือ must be switched off ส่วนรูป active ทำให้โทรศัพท์กลายเป็นผู้กระทำ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่หลัง Not only

topic.th: ความสอดคล้อง การเปรียบเทียบ และการสลับที่

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Not only ______ the competition, but she also broke the school record."

explanation.en: When "Not only" begins a sentence, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: "Not only did she win…". "She won" and "she did win" keep normal order, and "won she" inverts the main verb, which English does not allow.
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นประโยคด้วย Not only ต้องสลับกริยาช่วยมาไว้หน้าประธาน คือ did she win ส่วน she won และ she did win ยังเรียงแบบปกติ และ won she สลับกริยาแท้ซึ่งผิดหลัก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: causative have something done

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"My laptop screen was cracked, so I ______ at the shop near the station."

explanation.en: Someone at the shop fixed it for me, so we use the causative have + object + past participle: "had it repaired". "Had repaired it" says I fixed it myself; "had it repair" uses the wrong verb form.
explanation.th: ช่างที่ร้านเป็นผู้ซ่อมให้ จึงใช้ causative have + กรรม + V3 คือ had it repaired ส่วน had repaired it หมายถึงซ่อมเอง และ had it repair ใช้รูปกริยาผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: participle clause รูป Having + V3

topic.th: อนุประโยคสัมพันธ์และ participle clause

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"______ his homework, Tom went out to play football."

explanation.en: Tom finished first and then went out, and Tom is the doer, so the active perfect participle "Having finished" is right. "Finished" and the "being/been" forms are passive and would mean Tom was finished.
explanation.th: ทอมทำการบ้านเสร็จก่อนแล้วจึงออกไป และทอมเป็นผู้กระทำ จึงใช้ Having finished ส่วน Finished และรูปที่มี being/been เป็น passive ซึ่งความหมายผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: relative pronoun whose

topic.th: อนุประโยคสัมพันธ์และ participle clause

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The teacher ______ advice helped me most was Ms Anong."

explanation.en: The advice belongs to the teacher, and a noun (advice) follows the gap, so the possessive relative "whose" is needed. "Who", "whom" and "which" cannot be followed directly by a noun in this way.
explanation.th: คำแนะนำเป็นของครู และหลังช่องว่างเป็นคำนาม (advice) จึงต้องใช้ whose ซึ่งแสดงความเป็นเจ้าของ ส่วน who, whom, which ไม่สามารถตามด้วยคำนามแบบนี้ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Reported questions: word order and backshift

items.passage:
Why Teenagers Can't Fall Asleep Early

Many parents believe that teenagers stay up late simply because they are addicted to their phones or would rather chat with friends than rest. While screens certainly play a part, scientists now say that the main reason is biological. During puberty, the body begins to release melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, around two hours later than it did in childhood. As a result, a typical fifteen-year-old does not feel tired until eleven o'clock or even midnight, no matter how early he or she goes to bed.

This shift would not be a serious problem if teenagers could sleep later in the morning. Unfortunately, most secondary schools start their day between seven and eight o'clock, which means many students have to wake up at six or earlier. Doctors recommend that people aged thirteen to eighteen get between eight and ten hours of sleep a night, yet surveys in several countries show that fewer than one in three actually do. The missing hours add up quickly, and researchers call the result "sleep debt".

Sleep debt affects much more than how tired students feel. Studies have linked it to poorer memory, slower reaction times and difficulty controlling emotions. In some experiments, students who were short of sleep remembered far less of what they had learned the previous day than classmates who had slept well. There is also evidence that tired teenagers are more likely to have accidents on the road.

In response, a number of school districts in the United States have pushed back their start times to half past eight or later. The results have been encouraging: attendance has risen, fewer students fall asleep in class, and in some schools exam results have improved. Critics argue that later starts cause problems for parents who work early and for after-school sports, which must finish later in the evening. Nevertheless, supporters insist that these difficulties can be solved, whereas the effects of losing sleep cannot.

items.passage:
The Speech

Ploy had been practising her speech for three weeks, but as she stood behind the curtain of the school hall, every word seemed to have disappeared from her head. Through a gap in the curtain she could see the judges at a long table near the stage: two teachers from her own school and a visiting examiner from a language institute, who was writing something in a small notebook. Ploy's hands were shaking so badly that the paper with her notes rattled.

"Number seven, Ploy Srisuk," the announcer called.

She walked onto the stage and looked at the audience. Somewhere in the third row her grandmother was sitting, wearing the green silk scarf she saved for special occasions. Ploy had chosen to speak about her grandmother's life: how she had left her village at sixteen with almost no money, sold noodles from a cart in Bangkok for twenty years, and saved enough to send all four of her children to university.

For the first minute, Ploy's voice was so quiet that the people at the back leaned forward. Then she made a mistake. Instead of saying "she worked from dawn until dusk", she said "she worked from dusk until dawn". A few students laughed. Ploy's face burned, and for a terrible moment she thought about running off the stage.

Then she remembered something her grandmother had told her the night before. "When the noodles burn," her grandmother had said, "you don't throw away the whole pot. You smile at the customer and cook another bowl."

Ploy smiled. "Actually," she said, "that's not as wrong as it sounds. Some nights she really did work until dawn." This time the whole hall laughed with her, not at her, and suddenly the words came back. She finished the speech without looking at her notes once.

Ploy did not win first prize; that went to a boy from Matthayom 6 who had lived abroad for five years. But when she came down from the stage, the examiner stopped her and handed her a page torn from the small notebook. On it were four words: "Best recovery I've seen."
items.stem: Why were Ploy's hands shaking before she went on stage?
choices: She was angry with the judges.

explanation.en: Every word "seemed to have disappeared from her head" and she was about to perform, which shows nerves. Nothing suggests cold or anger, and she was holding her notes.

Subject: Summer Exchange Programme – application details

Dear Matthayom 4 students,

Our partner school in Nagoya, Japan, has invited eight students from our school to join its Summer Science Camp from 12 to 26 July. Students who take part will live with Japanese host families, attend morning classes in English, and spend the afternoons on field trips to research centres, factories and a national park.

To be eligible, you must:
• be a Matthayom 4 student in the English Program or the GATE Program in the current academic year;
• have a grade point average of at least 3.25 in the last semester;
• have no record of serious disciplinary problems.

Applications must include a one-page letter in English explaining why you want to join and what you hope to contribute, a recommendation from your homeroom teacher, and a consent form signed by a parent or guardian. Please note that letters longer than one page will not be read.

The partner school will cover tuition, meals at school and all field-trip costs. Families will be responsible for airfare (approximately 18,000 baht), travel insurance and personal spending money. A limited number of grants are available for students whose families would find these costs difficult; if you wish to apply for one, tick the box on the consent form and our finance office will contact you privately.

Shortlisted applicants will be interviewed in English on 15 March. The interview will last about ten minutes and will include a short discussion of a science news article, which you will be given twenty minutes to read beforehand. Dictionaries will not be allowed.

Completed applications should be handed in to Room 305 no later than 4:00 p.m. on Friday, 28 February. Late or incomplete applications will not be considered under any circumstances.

If you have any questions, please contact me by email rather than by phone, as I am teaching for most of the day.

Best wishes,
Ms Kanokwan Thepsiri
International Programmes Coordinator

choices: A Matthayom 5 English Program student with a GPA of 3.80
A Matthayom 4 GATE student with a GPA of 3.40
A Matthayom 4 regular-programme student with a GPA of 3.50
A Matthayom 4 English Program student with a GPA of 3.10

explanation.en: Applicants must be in Matthayom 4, in the EP or GATE Program, with a GPA of at least 3.25. Only the GATE student with 3.40 meets all three; the others are in the wrong year, the wrong programme, or below 3.25.

items.passage:
Close the Beaches — For a While

Every year, when the monsoon arrives, several of Thailand's most famous marine national parks close to visitors for four or five months. Tour operators complain, and some tourists are disappointed to find their dream island off-limits. I believe these closures are not only sensible but should be extended to more places, and perhaps made longer.

The case for closing parks is clearest at sites where nature had almost been destroyed before anyone acted. When one famous bay in the Andaman Sea was shut completely a few years ago, it had been receiving thousands of visitors a day. Boats had dropped anchor on the coral, and much of the reef was dead. Within a few years of the closure, scientists were reporting new coral growth, and reef sharks, which had almost vanished, returned in large numbers to the shallow water.

Opponents argue that closures hurt local people who depend on tourism for their income. This is a serious concern, and it would be wrong to dismiss it. But a beach with dead coral and no fish will not attract tourists for long either. In other words, protecting the environment is not the enemy of the tourism industry; it is the condition for its survival. Moreover, a well-managed reopening, with daily visitor limits and higher entrance fees, can bring in more money per visitor than an unlimited crowd ever did.

Some people also claim that closures are unfair because they punish today's tourists for the mistakes of the past. I find this argument weak. Nobody has a right to visit a fragile place whenever they like, any more than they have a right to walk through a hospital ward. Access to nature is a privilege, and privileges come with limits.

None of this means that every beach should be fenced off. Most coastlines can cope with visitors if rubbish is collected and boats are controlled. What I am arguing for is flexibility: parks should be allowed to close any area, for as long as necessary, whenever scientists say that it is in danger. If we wait until the damage is obvious to everyone, we will, once again, have waited too long.
items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: All Thai beaches should be closed permanently.
Tourism should be banned in national parks.
Temporary closures of fragile parks should be used more widely.
Monsoon closures are unnecessary and harm local people.

explanation.en: The writer supports closures and wants them "extended to more places", but the final paragraph says not every beach should be fenced off; the aim is flexible, temporary closures. Permanent closure of all beaches and a tourism ban go too far, and the writer defends monsoon closures.
explanation.th: ผู้เขียนสนับสนุนการปิดอุทยานและต้องการให้ขยายไปยังพื้นที่อื่น แต่ย่อหน้าสุดท้ายบอกว่าไม่ใช่ทุกชายหาดต้องปิด เป้าหมายคือการปิดชั่วคราวอย่างยืดหยุ่น การปิดถาวรทุกหาดหรือห้ามท่องเที่ยวจึงเกินไป และผู้เขียนเห็นด้วยกับการปิดช่วงมรสุม
